bib.title: PaSS: Parallel Speculative Sampling
bib.venue: 3rd Workshop on Efficient Natural Language and Speech Processing (NeurIPS 2023)

question: Can speculative sampling drafts come from the target model itself, via parallel decoding with a few learned look-ahead embeddings, instead of a second draft model?
hypothesis: Learning only L new input embeddings lets one forward pass of the frozen LLM draft L tokens well enough to speed up lossless decoding.
contributions: PaSS: speculative sampling whose draft comes from the target model through look-ahead embeddings, with no second model
Only O(d_emb) new parameters (L x d_emb), versus O(d_emb K) for look-ahead heads
Up to 30% speed-up on text and code completion with a 7B LLaMa

method.summary: Append L learned [LA] embeddings to the input so one forward pass of a frozen LLaMa-7B yields L draft tokens; a second pass validates them with the standard speculative-sampling rejection rule. Only the embeddings are trained.
method.task: lossless acceleration of autoregressive sampling (text and code completion)

datasets.name: English Wikipedia dump 2023/02/20
datasets.split: train/test split (proportions not stated); 200 random test examples for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: first 32 tokens of each test example used as prompt

datasets.name: The Stack (Python split)
datasets.split: train/test split (proportions not stated); 200 random test examples for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: first 32 tokens of each test example used as prompt

other.frozen: all parameters frozen except the new embeddings

training.objective: next-token loss on outputs at the look-ahead positions only; for each batch a random position is chosen to insert the look-ahead embeddings

other.which_L_trained: not stated whether one embedding set per L was trained for the L sweep

inference.decoding: top-k sampling with k = 10 (k = 25 for HumanEval Pass@10)
inference.temperature: 0.8 default; 0.5 and 0.2 in Table 1; 0.1 for Pass@1 and 0.8 for Pass@10 on HumanEval
inference.samples: 200 test examples per dataset; number of repeats or seeds not stated
inference.prompting: first 32 tokens of the example as prompt

parameters.look_ahead_tokens_L: 4 by default; 2, 4, 6, 8 swept on The Stack
parameters.kv_cache: used and updated after each call by drafted and accepted counts

other.speedup_bounds: lower bound is autoregressive wall time; upper bound (L+2)/2 x
other.calls_per_iteration: two LLM calls per iteration (draft, validate)

metrics.name: generation time
metrics.definition: time to generate a 512-token sequence from a 32-token prompt (Table 1); average time per HumanEval completion (Table 2)
metrics.unit: seconds in Table 2 (sec); Table 1 unit not printed

baselines: PaSS with a fixed [UNK] token as look-ahead instead of trained embeddings
eval.protocol: 200 random test examples per dataset; no seeds, variance or significance test stated; hardware for timing not stated

limits: Table 1 gives no time unit; no variance, seeds, or significance test; hardware not stated.
Only LLaMa 7B, one training set per task; dataset sizes and train/test split proportions not given.
No acceptance-rate or tokens-per-call numbers reported; speed-up is wall time only.
Gain saturates at about 6 look-ahead tokens; authors say draft quality of parallel generation is the main thing to improve.
Two model calls per iteration, so the (L+2)/2 upper bound is below the L+1 of classic speculative sampling.
HumanEval quality claim rests on equal Pass@k within 'margin of error' without an error estimate.
No comparison with a draft-model speculative sampling baseline or Medusa; only autoregressive and [UNK] baselines.

terms.definition: new tokens [LA]i appended to the input so the model predicts L positions ahead in one pass, with outputs from the original dictionary
a variant of speculative sampling that drafts candidate tokens via parallel decoding with look-ahead embeddings, needing no second model

code.snippet: accept draft x~_t if r < min(1, q(x~_t | x_1..x_{n+t-1}) / q(x~_t | x_1..x_{n-1}, [LA]_1..[LA]_t)); else sample from (q(.|...) - q(.|..., [LA]_1..[LA]_t))_+ and exit
